criteria.quote: Alakazam makes one-of-one spoons. Giving one requires trust.
criteria.revision: Open with the strongest contrast and delay the answer: “Alakazam uses psychic powers to make each spoon—and each one is said to be the only one of its kind in the whole world. Would it ever give one away?”

criteria.quote: Its spoons are said to be created by psychic powers.
criteria.revision: Replace the generic caption “EVERY SPOON MATTERS” with the concrete claim “EACH SPOON IS THE ONLY ONE OF ITS KIND,” keeping the focus on Alakazam’s psychic creation and worldwide uniqueness.

criteria.quote: Would Alakazam ever give away a spoon no one else has?
criteria.revision: Preserve this as the central open loop, but remove “Giving one requires trust” from the first scene and reveal the deep-trust condition only near the end.

criteria.quote: Its spoons are said to be created by psychic powers.
criteria.revision: Reorder the scenes so psychic creation and worldwide uniqueness establish the premise first, then escalate to the surprising possibility that Alakazam may let someone deeply trusted have one, followed by the apparently delicious food detail.

criteria.quote: A unique spoon can leave Alakazam's own hands.
criteria.revision: Withhold the gift until the reveal and use the exact stronger detail: “If it trusts someone deeply, it will let them have one of its spoons. Anything you eat with that spoon is apparently delicious.”
Cut the separate “SPOON-CHANGES-HANDS” scene because it repeats the later trust scene. Use that slot for the new information that anything eaten with the spoon is apparently delicious.

criteria.quote: Its spoon becomes a deeply personal gift: one original, shared through trust, for apparently delicious food.
criteria.revision: Make the ending resolve the opening question with the factual condition and consequence: “Yes—if Alakazam trusts someone deeply, it may give them a spoon no one else in the world has, and anything eaten with it is apparently delicious.”

criteria.quote: Would you treasure it, or use it for delicious meals?
criteria.revision: Sharpen the two credible choices while retaining the research-supported food detail: “Would you preserve the world’s only original—or use it, knowing anything eaten with it is apparently delicious?”
